newsitem.title: USA: First Central to miss some Aug. 1 payments.
newsitem.headline: First Central to miss some Aug. 1 payments.

text.p: First Central Financial Corp said Friday that it will not meet the August 1 interest and sinking fund obligations under its nine percent convertible subordinated debentures due 2000.
The company said it is negotiating with the largest holders of the debt.
The company has $4.9 million of outstanding debt. It owes a $1.8 million sinking fund payment and six months of interest at about $200,000, said company Controller Vincent Esposito.

The Lynbrook, N.Y.-based company is developing a plan to restructure and attract capital investors. The company's primary subsidiary, First Central Insurance Co, stopped writing new insurance business in March but continues to process renewals and service existing business.

"A capital investment is needed to enable First Central Insurance Co to resume normal operations. There is no assurance that First Central will successfully develop a restructuring plan or that it will be able to attract the necessary additional capital," a company statement said.
Esposito said the company is looking at various means of raising new capital and said there was no timeline as to when these efforts would bear fruit.
